subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Aquatics, Alternative, and Adapted Activity Options
essentialQuestion: What does an activity look like when it is designed for a different body than mine?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of water safety and aquatic activity where access exists in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe adapted and parasport activity forms using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving equipment adaptation and rule modification; correct it and explain why.
Connect access barriers: cost, transport, facility, and staffing with trying an activity form that is unfamiliar and reflecting honestly and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Trial two activity forms new to the learner — at least one adapted or alternative form — and produce an access analysis identifying what would make each sustainable.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Aquatics is optional and always substitutable; no learner is required to enter water. Every activity form has a dry-land, indoor, and zero-cost alternative.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
